_about: Ryan's picks of 9 October from the foeforge candidates, each source render kept beside this file at full size for later fixes (missing arms, weapons through hands). role: sprite (cut into art/foes at its frame), chibi (a hero's sprite for its domain's final, cut at 24x32), promoted (the boss register for the hero's promoted form, waiting on its entry). prompt is what rendered it; the seed is the candidate number. cut, where present, is the cutter's options that pick needed (a grey ground shadow wants --tol 90; sky between branches wants --holes).

goblin.prompt: 16-bit SNES JRPG battle sprite in the tradition of Final Fantasy VI, Chrono Trigger, Dragon Quest and Breath of Fire enemies: ornate, detailed, over-the-top high fantasy, menacing and played straight, never cute or comic, up to twenty colours, one-pixel dark outline. Full body, in three-quarter view turned toward the viewer's left (its right shoulder nearest the viewer), centered, isolated on a solid flat pure white background, no text, no border, no ground shadow. Subject: Goblin, a monster of the grasslands. The genre's first fight, with a knife. Every JRPG opens on one. The Meadow's rank and file. Small, loud and never alone: they come in sixes, straight at the nearest thing with a heartbeat, and the more of them stand the harder each one hits.  Light: the bright, saturated light of a sunny overworld field.
